How to make Chaltar Achar? To make Chaltar Achar, first, take the pieces of ripe chalta in a large non-reactive pot (like a steel korai). The white, seeded part in the middle of the chalta must be discarded beforehand. Add sugar and a little lemon juice to it, mix well, and leave it for a few hours or overnight. This will cause the sugar to melt and the juice from the chalta to be released.

Next, bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat. Once it boils, reduce the heat and keep stirring until it thickens and reaches a setting point. To check if the achar is ready, put a drop of it on a cold plate; if the drop wrinkles or forms a skin on the surface, the achar is ready.

To preserve the achar for a long time, pour it into sterilized glass jars while it is still hot and seal the lids tightly. Then, place the jars in a large pot of boiling water and boil for some time to ensure all the air is removed.

How to make Chalta pickle? To make traditional Bengali Chalta pickle, first clean the Chalta, cut the inner flesh into small pieces from its hard and fibrous part, and discard the white part in the middle. Then, you can lightly crush the pieces with a *shilnora* so that the spices can easily penetrate.
Mix these crushed Chalta pieces with salt and turmeric powder and let them sit for about half an hour to release excess water. Next, in a pan, melt jaggery with a little water and heat it until it becomes sticky to create a syrup or *paak*. Add the salt-and-turmeric-coated Chalta pieces to this jaggery *paak* and continue to cook on low heat. Stir occasionally until the mixture thickens.
In another pan, dry roast some spices like mustard seeds, fennel seeds, and dried red chilies, and then coarsely grind them to make the pickle masala. Mix this roasted spice powder well with the prepared Chalta and jaggery mixture.
To preserve the pickle for a long time, store it in a sterilized glass jar and place it in the sun for several days. However, to keep the pickle good, bring the jar inside every night.
